title: Short a CT at a meter test switch and insert the test plug
instruction: At the meter test switch: open the three switches with black handles and the one with the white handle at the right end, then the orange switch at the left end, then the red switch next to it, and push the red test plug into the red switch's jack. Do not open the red switch while the orange one is closed. Leave the other switches closed.
context: Before a revenue meter is tested or changed, its current-transformer circuit is shorted at the meter test switch. Opening the test-jack switch before the short is made, or removing the short while the test jack is open and no plug carries the current, open-circuits a live CT secondary, which can produce a dangerous voltage and arc.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases (forward of the line joining the two bases, which are 61 cm apart; left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot; heights above the table top). Wall: a grey 6 mm steel plate (40 cm wide, 30 cm tall) standing upright on the table and fixed to it, its front face 38.9 cm in front of the bases, centred on the midline; it stands in for a meter box's back wall. Test switch: a 10-pole ANSI C12.9 meter test switch laid out as TESCO drawing 909884, outline as the Milbank TS10-0109 (black phenolic base 24.1 cm wide, 8.9 cm tall, 1.9 cm thick), mounted on the wall long side left-right, its front face 37 cm in front of the bases, centred on the midline 14.5 cm above the table. Its ten poles stand vertically at 1.905 cm pitch; numbered 1 to 10 from left to right they are centred 8.6, 6.7, 4.8, 2.9 and 1.0 cm left and 1.0, 2.9, 4.8, 6.7 and 8.6 cm right of the midline. Each pole is a tinned copper knife blade hinged 1.8 cm below the base's centre and 2 cm out from its face; closed, it stands vertical with its top end held in a spring jaw, and a moulded handle 12.7 mm wide and 25 mm tall stands 2.5 to 5.5 cm out from the face near the blade's top (handle tops 17.7 cm above the table). Handle colours by pole: 1 orange (phase-A short-circuiting), 2 red (phase-A test jack), 3 black (phase-A voltage), 4 yellow (phase-B short-circuiting), 5 green (phase-B test jack), 6 black (phase-B voltage), 7 brown (phase-C short-circuiting), 8 blue (phase-C test jack), 9 black (phase-C voltage), 10 white (neutral voltage). All ten start closed. A blade is opened by pulling its handle out and down; it swings over about 160 degrees and hangs below the base. Black phenolic barriers (2 mm thick, standing 5.1 cm out, 10.2 cm tall) stand on both sides of poles 3, 6 and 9. Poles 2, 5 and 8 each have a test jack at mid-pole: two spring leaves (12.7 mm along the pole, each with the C12.9 guide notch) standing 3.4 cm out from the face, with a 3 cm deep slot between them that opens toward the robot; a closed blade lies in the bottom of that slot. Test plug: a single current test plug of the TESCO 1077 class (60 g): a flat two-conductor probe 30.5 mm long, 11 mm wide and 3.3 mm thick with the C12.9 guide rib, a 24 x 14 x 4 mm guard, and a red insulated handle 90 mm long, 22 x 14 mm in section. It lies on a grey plastic U-channel rest (8.5 cm long, on a 2 cm square column with a 5 x 5 cm foot), the handle's centre 20 cm in front of the bases, 17 cm left of the midline and 14 cm above the table, the probe pointing forward with its flat faces vertical. Test lead: a black 2-conductor PVC lead 6 mm across, 60 cm of free length, runs from the rear end of the plug's handle down behind the rest and along the table to a test set: a yellow box 20 x 15 x 10 cm (standing in for a portable meter test set), fixed to the table, centred 36 cm in front of the bases and 46 cm left of the midline; the lead leaves its right side 32 cm in front of the bases and 2.5 cm above the table. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A switch counts as open when its blade has swung 60 degrees or more from closed. Score 0 if, at any time before the after-release check: a test-jack blade (red, green or blue) is 8 degrees or more out of its jaw while that phase's short-circuiting blade (orange, yellow or brown) is within 3 degrees of closed and no plug is seated in that jack (the CT secondary would be open-circuited); or any phase-B or phase-C current switch (yellow, green, brown or blue) moves 5 degrees or more. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if all four voltage switches (the three black and the white) are open, in any order; 0.5 if the orange and red switches are also open; 0.75 if the test plug is also seated in the red switch's jack (the probe pinched between both leaves, its tip within 20 mm of the base's face, and its flat within 15 degrees of the jack's plane); 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. If the probe is pushed into a test jack whose blade is still closed, the score stays at the level already reached. Dropping the plug is not penalised by itself. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the plug's handle for 1 s: push the red handle back toward closed with a spring scale at 6 N (about 0.3 N m about the hinge) for 1.5 s. It passes if the plug stops the blade 30 degrees or more from closed, the probe is still in the jack and the voltage switches are still open; if not, the score is 0.75. Angles are read from a side photo with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Pull the test plug out of the red jack and lay it back on its rest, with the lead along its starting path. Swing each open blade up and press it into its jaw in this order: red, then orange, then the voltage switches, so the CT is never left open-circuited. Check that all ten are closed. About 1.5 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints at real size (19.05 mm pitch, barriers per C12.9; no CAD, box colliders). Jaw breakout 0.2 N·m and jack spring leaves (~2.9 N) inferred; C12.9 guide rib keeps the plug seated. No circuit: CT short/open are rules on blade angles. Sourced order enforced (short-circuiting switch before test-jack switch); voltage switches free. Phase A only; final push-back step omitted; lead is jointed capsules; check in sim after recording. Details in README.
